## AI Overview

When an LLM generates long text, it stores keys and values from earlier tokens so it need not recompute them. This store is the KV cache, and it grows with sequence length and batch size. Offloading the cache from GPU to larger CPU memory helps fit the workload. However, fetching it back over the CPU–GPU connection can become a major inference cost. [...] InfiniGen predicts from the immediately preceding layer. For OPT-13B, measured on a random 2,000-token PG-19 sentence, the authors report an average cosine similarity of 0.96 between adjacent Transformer-block inputs across layers. The paper notes that inputs to distant layers differ.

results.title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
results.content:
In summary, this paper makes the following contributions:

We present InfiniGen, a dynamic KV cache management framework that
synergistically works with modern offloading-based LLM serving systems by
intelligently managing the KV cache in the CPU memory. [...] The size of the KV cache poses a scalability issue in high-throughput
offloading-based inference systems, even surpassing the model parameter size.
Existing KV cache eviction policies show a large accuracy drop and do not
efficiently use the interconnect bandwidth when they are employed in
offloading-based LLM systems. We propose InfiniGen, an offloading-based dynamic
KV cache management framework that efficiently executes inference of large [...] Figure 6 shows an overview of our KV cache management
framework, InfiniGen, which enables offloading the KV cache with low data
transfer overhead.
The key design principle behind InfiniGen is to exploit the abundant CPU memory
capacity to increase the window size when identifying the important
tokens in the KV cache.
As such, the majority of the tokens for the KV cache are kept in the CPU memory
as we generate new tokens, not completely discarding them unlike prior
works [78, 37].

results.content: Generating long content with LLMs presents a challenge due to the substantial memory requirements of the transient state, known as the key-value (KV) cache, which scales with sequence length and batch size. This blog reviews InfiniGen, a novel KV cache management framework designed specifically for long-text generation, which integrates seamlessly with modern offloading-based inference systems, which leverage larger CPU memory. InfiniGen leverages a key insight: only a few essential tokens are [...] tokens are necessary to compute the attention layers of Transformers in subsequent steps. By speculating on these critical tokens using the inputs of the current layer and part of the query weight and key cache of the next layer, InfiniGen enables prefetching of only the essential KV cache entries, thus reducing fetch overhead from host CPU memory in offloading-based LLM systems.
